name: Microsoft Azure ND H100 v5 (ND96isr, 8x H100)
price_basis: per H100 GPU-hour. ND96isr H100 v5 = 8x H100, Linux on-demand $98.32/instance-hr / 8 = $12.29 in eastus. Spot $18.169536 = $2.2712. Low Priority $19.664 = $2.458. Reservation meter $551,221/h normalised, i.e. ~$62.88/instance-hr = ~$7.86/GPU-hr (~$36% off). A second Consumption meter for the same SKU reads $102.736 and Windows meters read $102.736; the Linux no-pre-installed-software meter is used. Fetched from the Retail Prices API 2026-10-03.
notes: Tied with Google a3 as the most expensive on-demand H100 hour in this slice, and there is a GENUINE CONFLICT WITH THE PRICING PAGE that must be understood before booking: the rendered Azure VM pricing page lists ND96isr H100 v5 as $71,773.60 per MONTH, whereas the Retail Prices API says $98.32 per HOUR. Those are not reconcilable (98.32 x 730 = $71,773.60 exactly - so the 'monthly' figure is simply the hourly rate times 730 hours and is a display artifact, not a discount). Do not read $71,773 as a monthly commitment price. Azure's reservation model is the real discount and it is unusually deep: the API's normalised Reservation meter works out to roughly $7.86/GPU-hour at 1 year, about 36% off, though the pricing page shows '-' in both the 1-year and 3-year savings-plan columns for this SKU, so treat the derived reservation figure as indicative rather than offered. Spot is the standout: $2.27 per H100-hour is ~82% off on-demand and is the cheapest H100 hour from any hyperscaler in this slice - better than Lambda's on-demand - but it is interruptible, Azure evicts both for capacity reallocation and for exceeding your max price, and you must set a max price in USD. Hardware: 96 vCPU, 1,900 GiB RAM, 28,000 GiB temp storage, NVLink 4.0 in-VM and a dedicated 400 Gb/s Quantum-2 CX7 InfiniBand link per GPU with GPUDirect RDMA - 3.2 Tb/s per VM, the best per-GPU scale-out fabric of any instance here. No contract required to deploy; a credit card and an Azure account suffice.
